html:
Tocobaga was a chiefdom at the head of Old Tampa Bay, on the Gulf coast of Florida, known from Spanish accounts of the 1500s. The name served for the chiefdom, its chief and its main town, probably the mound site in today's Safety Harbor.

Its people fished, gathered shellfish and built platform mounds; archaeologists call their way of life the Safety Harbor culture, which took shape around 900. Spanish expeditions came one after another. The Narváez expedition landed near Tampa Bay in 1528, and Hernando de Soto in 1539. In 1567 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés made peace between Tocobaga and its rival to the south, the Calusa, and left a small garrison; the soldiers were soon killed. Disease and slave raids from the north emptied the Tampa Bay region by the early 1700s, during the years of Spanish Florida.
